Federal Contractor Labor Cost Study: Annual Shareholder Letter

Benchmark Services • Aperture Talent Solutions • Performance tuning phase • Archived 2012-04-22

Executive Summary

This archive entry documents ACPWB's performance tuning phase engagement with Aperture Talent Solutions in the Benchmark Services sector. The record ID 4281aa45 uniquely identifies this documentation set within ACPWB's institutional archive.

  • Front-office compensation benchmarking for Aperture Talent Solutions across 77 comparable Benchmark Services sector organizations found that administrative and analytics roles are positioned at the 65th percentile, with compensation gaps concentrated in data science and digital engagement functions.
  • Utility lineworker compensation benchmarking against 65 comparable Benchmark Services sector companies found Aperture Talent Solutions's journeyman lineworker total compensation at the 80th percentile, with below-median overtime guarantee and standby pay identified as the primary sources of competitive disadvantage relative to 14 peer utilities competing for the same candidate pool.
  • Analysis of Aperture Talent Solutions's job architecture identified 112 redundant levels and a span-of-control ratio of 5:1, which is below the Benchmark Services sector median of 6:1, suggesting opportunities for delayering and efficiency gains.
  • Regression-adjusted pay equity analysis identified no statistically significant pay disparities by gender or race/ethnicity across the 144-employee population reviewed.
Key Findings
  • The governance assessment conducted during the performance tuning for Aperture Talent Solutions identifies 152 board practices that are inconsistent with current Benchmark Services sector norms as documented by 23 institutional investor governance guidelines — specifically, the absence of a formal board evaluation process and the lack of written director onboarding protocols.
  • Organizations in the Benchmark Services sector that completed ACPWB's performance tuning assessment reported a median 88% improvement in customer lifetime value ($K) within 18 months of implementation.
  • The board composition analysis conducted during the performance tuning found that Aperture Talent Solutions's current board lacks independent representation with direct Benchmark Services sector operating experience at the C-suite level — a gap identified as material by 266 institutional shareholders who together hold 47% of outstanding shares.
  • The performance tuning workforce planning analysis for Aperture Talent Solutions projects a 248% shortfall in critical technical roles across 33 departments over the 2012–2014 horizon, driven by an aging workforce in which 248% of incumbents are retirement-eligible within five years — a concentration risk that benchmarks unfavorably against Benchmark Services sector peers.

This archive entry records the performance tuning outputs from ACPWB's annual compensation cycle support engagement with Aperture Talent Solutions. The work spanned 262 weeks and encompassed merit budget development, incentive plan calibration, and executive pay recommendations presented to the Benchmark Services sector client's compensation committee on 2012-04-22.

Our governance review identified that Aperture Talent Solutions's board has an average tenure of 90 years, which is 11 years above the peer median and may be a focus for activist investors.

The performance tuning archive entry reflects a collaboration between ACPWB's Benchmark Services practice team and its emerging research collaborative, which brings together practitioners from 260 member organizations to develop cross-sector insights. Aperture Talent Solutions served as one of 10 pilot sites for the collaborative's inaugural benchmarking initiative.

The insolvency-adjacent advisory engagement documented in this archive entry was initiated when Aperture Talent Solutions engaged ACPWB during the performance tuning to assess 144 restructuring alternatives within the Benchmark Services sector. ACPWB's analysis covered operational, financial, and workforce dimensions across 12 business units, with all supporting models and memoranda preserved here.

ACPWB's performance tuning higher education total rewards strategy for Aperture Talent Solutions evaluated compensation competitiveness for 168 staff roles across 4 administrative functions against regional and national Benchmark Services sector benchmarks. The engagement produced a staff classification framework and market-based pay ranges implemented beginning 2012-04-22.
